title: shulker.json
description: Shulker project manifest. Lists direct mods, the sides it builds, and first-class configuration. Resolution results live in shulker.lock.

name.description: Project name. Used in messages and as the default instance name for launchers.

version.description: Pack version shown to people, e.g. "1.0" or "2026-09". Never parsed. Used as the versionId of an exported .mrpack and in its file name.

description.description: One paragraph about the pack, shown to players. First paragraph of the ModMenu entry and, joined with note, the summary of an exported .mrpack.

authors.description: Shown by ModMenu as "by ..." under the project name. init seeds the git user.name and shulker.sh; delete entries freely.

license.description: The project's license, e.g. "MIT" or "CC BY-NC-SA 4.0". Shown on the project's entry in the mod list, and clickable there when links.license is set. Defaults to "All rights reserved", since NeoForge and Forge reject a mod that declares no license.

minecraft.description: Semver range over Minecraft version ids, e.g. "~26.2", "^26.1", or an exact version. Pre-release order is snapshot < pre < rc < release. Omit it to take the version from the project's locked modpacks, which then all have to agree.

java.description: Optional override. Either an absolute path to a JDK/JRE home or a semver range over the Java major version, e.g. ">=25". Omit to derive from the Minecraft version json and use the managed runtime.

providers.description: Provider preference order. A single entry makes the tool single-provider.

features.description: Optional parts of the pack, each one switch over the mods gated with feature and over the feature's own override folder. --with and --without decide a feature for one build; feature on and feature off record the choice.

requires.description: Mods, modpacks, resource packs and shaders this project requires, in one map keyed by a name unique across them. A mod's key is its in-jar mod id; a resource pack's or shader's key is the file name it is placed under, so a pack enabled in game stays enabled when it updates. An entry with source is a modpack whose mods and overrides merge into this project; an empty entry is a mod at the newest release-channel file for the locked Minecraft and loader.

ignore.description: Per-pair overrides for unmet depends or matched breaks found in jar metadata.

wholeFiles.description: Build-relative paths or globs (* and ? match within one path segment) of .properties overrides to copy whole. Other .properties overrides merge per key: only the keys they list are managed, and keys a mod adds are left alone.

marker.description: Include the marker mod in a client build: the pack's own entry in the in-game mod list, which also lets an export of the build be recognised as this pack again. Off drops both, and exports also leave out the shulker.json and shulker.lock they carry at the archive root and the CurseForge profile image. Default true. An instance that sets its own settings.marker decides for itself instead.

history.description: How many history entries `history prune` leaves, and the count a build warns above. An instance takes an entry before anything it manages changes: the manifest and lock before a relock saves them, and the files before a build writes over ones you edited. -1 keeps every entry and never warns; 0 takes none.

links.description: Links shown on the project's ModMenu entry. website, issues, and source become the Website, Issues, and Source buttons. A key ModMenu knows (discord, modrinth, curseforge, wiki, youtube, reddit, twitter, mastodon, twitch, patreon, kofi, paypal, donate, ...) uses its label; any other key is shown as written. On NeoForge and Forge, where the entry has room for less, website and issues become the Homepage and Issues buttons and license makes the license clickable.

note.description: Free-text documentation. The comment substitute; ignored by the tool.

osCondition.description: An operating system name, or !name to exclude it.

featureCondition.description: A feature name, or !name to require it off.

modId.description: In-jar mod id as declared in fabric.mod.json, quilt.mod.json or neoforge.mods.toml.

projectId.description: Provider project id. Modrinth ids are base62 strings, CurseForge ids are integers.

versionId.description: Provider version id. Modrinth version ids are base62 strings, CurseForge file ids are integers.

loader.description: The mod loader. Omitted means no loader: vanilla Minecraft, which takes no mods.

version.description: Semver range over the loader's own version. "*", the default when omitted, selects the newest for the locked Minecraft version.

relativePath.description: Path relative to the project root, forward slashes, no leading slash. The tool rejects .. segments.

variables.description: Values substituted for ${name} in *.tmpl override files and in server.properties values.

default.description: Whether the feature is on when nothing else decides it. A recorded choice, --with and --without all win over it.

overrides.description: Override folder this feature adds while it is on, layered after the base folders in feature name order. A string is one folder for both sides; an object gives a folder per side, either key alone. Defaults to <name>-overrides/.

requireKey.description: Name of a requires entry, unique across mods, modpacks, resource packs and shaders. Used in messages and requiredBy, and as the placed file name for a resource pack or shader.

type.description: What the entry is. Omitted means modpack for an entry with source and mod otherwise, unless the provider says otherwise; when given it must agree with the entry. Resource packs and shaders are resolved from the provider's own project type and placed in resourcepacks/ or shaderpacks/.

source.description: Local path, git URL, or raw manifest URL of a modpack.

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit for a git source. The lock records the resolved commit.

autoUpdate.description: Whether sync refreshes this modpack from its source, or re-reads its archive when the archive's bytes change. Omitted means true; false pins the modpack at its locked state. update refreshes every modpack regardless.

locked.description: Whether the modpack's mods are copied verbatim from its lock, dependencies included, instead of resolved against this project. Omitted means true when the source has a lock, and always for an archive, which pins exact files; a source without a lock is always resolved from its manifest.

file.description: A local jar or zip that is on no provider, placed like any other entry of its kind. On a modpack, a .mrpack archive: its mods lock as the modpack's and its override folders become the modpack's layers. The lock records its sha512, and changed bytes make the lock out of date.

filename.description: Resource packs and shaders only: the file name the pack is placed under, in place of <key>.zip. The game enables packs by file name, so this keeps a pack enabled under a name players already use. Unique within its folder whatever the case.

project.description: Written by add when the provider slug differs from the mod id or the provider is CurseForge.

pin.description: Pin to one provider version. update skips pinned mods.

channel.description: Least stable channel accepted. A channel admits itself and anything more stable.

side.description: Overrides the side derived from provider environment data.

provider.description: Overrides the provider preference list for this mod.

os.description: Ship only on these operating systems, evaluated where the build runs. Names are any-of, !names are none-of; both must hold. A dependency needed only by excluded mods is excluded too.

feature.description: Ship only when a feature is on. Names are any-of, !names are none-of; both must hold, together with os. Every name must be declared in features, which is where its default lives.

mod.description: The mod whose jar metadata declares the constraint.

on.description: Subject of the constraint: a mod id or one of the built-ins minecraft, java, fabricloader, quilt_loader, neoforge, forge.

declared.description: The range exactly as the jar declared it when this ignore was written. A jar that declares a different range makes the ignore stale and the original failure re-surfaces.

note.description: Why this constraint is safe to ignore. Required.

player.description: A player by name, uuid, or both. The lock stores both after resolution.

serverProperties.description: Keys written into server.properties. Values may reference ${variables}. Known keys are listed for completion (verified against the 26.2 table on 2026-09-10); the tool validates the full set against the locked Minecraft version.

level-name.description: World folder name. Also selects which world under data/ is linked into the server build.

name.description: Display name launchers show for this side (Prism instance name, official launcher profile name). Defaults to the manifest name.

build.description: Output directory. Defaults to build/<side>; "." builds into the project directory itself, which is what makes the project an instance.

eula.description: eula.txt is written only when true. serve refuses to start otherwise.

jvmFlags.description: JVM flags preset used by serve. aikars applies Aikar's G1 flags (12 GB+ variant chosen from memory, -Xms set equal to -Xmx); none passes only the memory flags.

jvmArgs.description: Extra JVM arguments appended after the preset, e.g. ZGC flags.

clientHooks.description: What a launcher instance of this pack does around a launch, by default. These seed settings.hooks when the instance is created; the instance decides from then on, and a link flag overrides them once.

preLaunch.description: Sync the instance from this project before each launch. Default true.

postExit.description: Record how each run ended when the game exits. Default true.

name.description: Display name launchers show for this side (Prism instance name, official launcher profile name). Defaults to the manifest name.

build.description: Output directory. Defaults to build/<side>; "." builds into the project directory itself, which is what makes the project an instance.

options.description: Keys written into options.txt as key:value. Other keys already in the file are left alone.

ip.description: host or host:port, as typed into the multiplayer screen.
